verses.text: The high priest asked Stephen, “Are these accusations true?”
Stephen replied, “Brothers and fathers, hear me. The glorious God appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran.
“God told him, ‘Leave your land and your relatives. Go to the land I will show you.’
“So Abraham left the Chaldeans’ land and settled in Haran. After his father died, God brought him here, to the land where you now live.
“God gave him no inheritance here—not even enough ground to stand on. But God promised to give the land to him and to his descendants, even though Abraham had no child yet.
“God told him that his descendants would live as foreigners in another land, where people would enslave and mistreat them for four hundred years.
“God also said, ‘I will judge the nation that enslaves them. Afterward they will leave and worship me in this place.’

“Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision. Abraham became Isaac’s father and circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac became Jacob’s father, and Jacob became the father of the twelve patriarchs.
“The patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt. But God was with him
“and rescued him from all his troubles. God gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, who appointed him governor over Egypt and his whole household.
“Then a famine and severe hardship struck all Egypt and Canaan, and our ancestors couldn’t find food.
“When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for the first time.
“When they went a second time, Joseph revealed who he was to his brothers, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph’s family.
“Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives—seventy-five people in all.
“Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our ancestors died.
“They were brought back to Shechem and placed in the tomb Abraham had bought with silver from Hamor’s family in Shechem.
“As the time drew near for God to fulfill his promise to Abraham, our people had become numerous in Egypt.
“Then a new king came to power, one who knew nothing about Joseph.
“He took advantage of our people and cruelly mistreated our ancestors, forcing them to abandon their babies so they wouldn’t survive.
“At that time Moses was born. He was exceptionally beautiful before God and was cared for at his father’s home for three months.
“When he was left outside, Pharaoh’s daughter took him in and raised him as her own son.
“Moses was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians and became powerful in what he said and did.
“When Moses was forty, he decided to visit his fellow Israelites.
“He saw one of them being mistreated, stepped in to defend him, and struck down the Egyptian who was hurting him.
“Moses thought his people would understand that God was using him to rescue them, but they didn’t.
“The next day he saw two Israelites fighting. He tried to make peace, saying, ‘Men, you’re brothers. Why are you hurting each other?’
“But the man harming his neighbor pushed Moses away and said, ‘Who put you in charge of us as ruler and judge?
“‘Are you going to kill me like you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
“When Moses heard that, he fled and lived as a foreigner in Midian, where he had two sons.
“Forty years later, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness near Mount Sinai, in the flame of a burning bush.
“Moses was amazed by what he saw. As he came closer to look, the Lord’s voice spoke to him:
“‘I am the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled and didn’t dare look.
“The Lord told him, ‘Take off your sandals. The place where you’re standing is holy ground.
“‘I have seen how my people are suffering in Egypt. I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. Now come—I’m sending you to Egypt.’
“This is the same Moses whom the people rejected by asking, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ God sent him as both ruler and rescuer, with the help of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
“He led them out, performing wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
“This is the Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up a prophet like me for you from among your own people.’
“He was with our people in the wilderness assembly, with the angel who spoke to him at Mount Sinai and with our ancestors. He received living words to pass on to us.
“But our ancestors refused to obey him. They pushed him away and turned their hearts back toward Egypt.
“They told Aaron, ‘Make gods to lead us. We don’t know what happened to this Moses who brought us out of Egypt.’
“They made a calf idol in those days, offered sacrifices to it, and celebrated what their own hands had made.

“So God turned away from them and let them worship the stars in the sky, just as the prophets’ book says: ‘People of Israel, did you bring me offerings and sacrifices during those forty years in the wilderness?
“‘You carried the shrine of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, idols you made to worship. So I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’
“Our ancestors had the tent of the covenant in the wilderness. God had instructed Moses to make it according to the pattern he had seen.
“Our ancestors received the tent from those who came before them and brought it with Joshua when they took possession of the nations God drove out ahead of them. It stayed there until David’s time.
“David found favor with God and asked to build a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
“But Solomon built a house for him.
“Still, the Most High doesn’t live in houses built by human hands. As the prophet says:
“‘Heaven is my throne, and the earth is under my feet. What kind of house could you build for me?’ says the Lord. ‘Where could I rest?
“‘Didn’t I make all these things with my own hand?’
“You are stubborn, with hearts and ears that are uncircumcised! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your ancestors did.
“Which prophet did your ancestors not persecute? They killed those who announced the coming of the Righteous One. And now you have betrayed and murdered him.
“You received the law delivered by angels, but you haven’t kept it!”
When the council heard this, they were furious and ground their teeth at Stephen.
But Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked up into heaven and saw God’s glory, with Jesus standing at God’s right hand.
He said, “Look! I see heaven opened, and the Son of Man standing at God’s right hand!”
They shouted loudly, covered their ears, and rushed at Stephen together.
They dragged him outside the city and stoned him. The witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
As they stoned Stephen, he called out, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit!”
He knelt and cried out loudly, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” After saying this, he died.
